Your new workspace expects the audience https://sso.meridian.example/saml/ws_8p2m7x, but Okta is sending the one for your main workspace, ws_4k9d2a. traces.reply: Hi Galloway Mutual Insurance team, yes, there is an overlap period. In Settings > API keys, click Rotate next to the key. Meridian creates a new key with the same scopes, and the old key keeps working for 24 hours so you can deploy the new key without downtime. After 24 hours the old key stops working and returns 401 Unauthorized. Copy the new key when it is shown, since it appears only once. Store it in a secrets manager or environment variables. If a key was ever exposed publicly, revoke it instead of rotating, because revoking takes effect right away. Full steps are in [KB-006]. A support engineer will follow up if you have more questions.

assessment.rationale: The customer computes the HMAC over JSON.stringify(req.body) instead of the raw request body, which is cause #1 in KB-013, so this is a setup issue rather than a Meridian signing defect. The fix is to verify against the raw bytes; a single integration is affected and it is not yet in production.

decision.reason: A how-to, configuration, or billing issue with a high-confidence article match resolves.
evidence: KB-013 matched with high confidence

traces.reply: Hi Driftwood Ticketing, the signing is most likely fine. The mismatch comes from computing the HMAC over JSON.stringify(req.body). Once your framework has parsed the JSON, re-serializing it changes spacing and key order, so the result won't match. The signature is calculated over the raw request body, so configure your Node route to give you the raw bytes (before any JSON parsing) and compute the HMAC-SHA256 on that, then compare with a constant-time check. It also helps to strip any whitespace or newlines from the secret when you load it. You can confirm the fix with Send test event in Settings > Webhooks. Full steps are in [KB-013]. If it still fails after that, a support engineer will follow up.
